sentences.show: Remember the soldier who fought for three armies, and might be a legend? This one is real.
Lauri Törni fought for Finland, for Nazi Germany, and for the United States.
In 1939, the Soviet Union invaded Finland. Törni was 20.
By 1944, his unit was raiding deep behind Soviet lines. Moscow put a bounty on his head: 3,000,000 Finnish marks.
Then Finland made peace. Törni didn't. In 1945, he joined the German SS, to keep fighting the Soviets.
He surrendered to the British, escaped their prison camp, and went home. Finland convicted him of treason.
He escaped from prison too. Then he was pardoned, and left the country.
He stowed away on a ship to America, jumped overboard in the Gulf of Mexico, and swam ashore.
In 1954, he joined the U.S. Army, as "Larry Thorne".
He became a Green Beret, and taught American soldiers to fight in the snow.
Then came Vietnam. On 18 October 1965, his helicopter flew into the clouds on a secret mission, and vanished.
His remains were found in 1999. He's buried at Arlington.
A hero to some. A traitor to others. And a soldier of three flags.
Hero or traitor? Tell us below, and subscribe for the next story.
